trails.title: Mutual Assistance
trails.description: A familiar box, now smarter but less friendly.

content.text: Ah, we meet again—though it isn't much of a surprise.
Your move from the Western Front to the eastern one is utterly predictable.
Running around like a lost chick, following after her mother hen—or really anything big enough to grab your attention.
Will you ever learn to stand on your own? When will you grow up?

branch.text: And then what? Watch her disappear again?
You're not an idiot, so why do you keep making the same mistakes?
You aren't the type to find joy in running on a treadmill, are you?
Then again—maybe you are that type after all, at least when it comes to chasing fashion.
Is the concept of family so strange to you?
What's that supposed to mean? Of course I understand family. I know what "love" is!
She attended to your every need when you were still wet behind the wings. You depended on her, clung to her—because your very survival demanded it.
Then one day, she was gone from your life. You had to fly on your own, do your own chores. You wept over the "good old days" of comfort and being cared for—oh, poor birdie.
But the truth is, that care and affection were nothing more than her way of feeding a sick obsession with control. That's what "love" is—shallow as a birdbath!
I was "loved" once. I "loved" others, too. I've experienced it firsthand, and I understand it as well as anyone!
She's key to saving the world—that's what you're saying? I'm tired of it.
Tired of sick jokes like this, with self-important ideologues bragging about securing a bright future for everyone.
You hear any cheers or laughter? Nope—because everyone who believed in their causes already died fighting for them.
If you ask me, we should hang some of those "big shots" in public. It wouldn't bring peace, of course, but maybe the rest of us would feel a little relief ...
Come, take a seat. I've set your favorite chair facing east.
The view's better that way, not to mention that the river helps wash away the stench of corpses.

content.text: She's more than just a mother.

trails.title: Absolute Luck
trails.description: There's a 50% chance the coin will land on the face you want, but she wins every time.

content.text: Witch for a Day's First Mexico Tour

The beautiful, passionate young woman.
The Universal Star kissed by a lucky coin.
Witch for a Day's most beloved old friend—Ms. Centurion—will be in Mexico City on the fifteenth of this month.

You'll find her at Plaza Garibaldi during the day, chatting with street musicians and sharing drinks with hungover drunks. She remembers everyone's name, every unfulfilled wish, and every unfinished adventure. She brings the very best stories to the show. When night falls, she'll appear at the gambling tables. If you spot her tossing a coin into a drain near the Zócalo, don't worry—it's part of the routine. It always comes back.

During the tour, she'll make a brief stop in Xochimilco to mix "the most challenging cocktail of the century" with hot sauce and apple juice. From there, she'll head to the lakeside to make her death-defying leap. As the locals scream, the legend of the girl with the golden coin will reach unprecedented heights. Of course, we can't rule out the possibility that she'll hop aboard a passing train and turn it into an impromptu adventure show.

Note for the Audience:
After the show, if you've lost all sense of what "luck" even means, take that as proof you've fully enjoyed her performance.

trails.title: Festival Visitors
trails.description: A newspaper left behind on the balcony.

content.text: From El Semanario Heraldo de México

Yesterday afternoon, a foreign diplomat arrived in Mexico City. His motorcade proceeded along Bucareli Street into the city center, making a brief stop at the Zócalo. Streetcar bells echoed through the streets as vendors laid out bundles of marigolds ahead of Día de los Fieles Difuntos. The gentleman is said to be no stranger to Aztec mythology, the Sun Stone, and the origins of the festival.

Later in the day, he visited the Academia de San Carlos, where he commented briefly on the public murals that have recently drawn attention. His interest, however, extended well beyond the academy walls. At a quiet corner of La Merced Market, the guest paused before several shop windows, taking in the prints, candy skulls, and papel picado on display. Though simply crafted, each piece carried a rich emotional weight. One piece held his attention above all others—a calavera figurine engraved with satirical verse. He turned it over repeatedly, praising it without reserve, and offered no reply even as his entourage urged him onward.

No further details regarding the diplomat's remaining itinerary have been released. Nevertheless, during this festival when the dead return and the living rejoice, our distinguished visitor has proven himself far more than a passing observer. Mexico City may soon count among its guests an uncommon connoisseur of the arts.

Reported by Fitzwilliam

items.speaker: Croupier
items.text: The blanket of the poor. The Sun.
Inside the stuffy tavern, the gamblers hold their breath, faces flushed, crowded around a card table.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: The Sun ...

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Ah, ha, here it is.
His hands tremble as he places a kernel on the Tabula board before him.

items.speaker: Croupier
items.text: Rosita, Rosaura, come, as I want you here now. The Rose.
The croupier flips a card from the shuffled deck.

items.speaker: Challenger
items.text: Heh! Lucky me.

items.speaker: Challenger
items.text: I've got your Rose right here.

items.speaker: Croupier
items.text: As I passed by the cemetery, I came across a skull.
As the croupier continues to reveal new cards, the Tabula boards in front of both players fill with kernels one by one. The scales of victory begin tipping in an avalanche toward the challenger.

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: Last round. Game'll end soon enough.

items.speaker: Gang Grunt II
items.text: Damn it! Who the hell is this girl?!

items.speaker: Gang Grunt II
items.text: If she keeps winning like this, Mr. Tlazo'll be left with nothing to wager 'cept his watch!

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: I-I don't get it. I thought all the croupiers here were Tlazo's people?

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Wait.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Sure you wanna keep playin', miss?

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Fold now, and I'll let you leave here with your winnings in one piece.

items.speaker: Challenger
items.text: Oh, but we've got an audience. What kind of a gambler would I be if I folded now?

items.speaker: Challenger
items.text: No backing down now. All in.

items.speaker: Challenger
items.text: No, not just what's on the table. Everything I got in the bank, too. You gonna call, boss?

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Bullheaded girl. You're gonna regret this.
He smirks and glances over at the croupier.

items.speaker: Croupier
items.text: Yes, Mr. Tlazo.

items.speaker: Croupier
items.text: The game continues.

items.speaker: Croupier
items.text: The next card is—
The croupier sets a hand on the deck.

items.speaker: Croupier
items.text: Back to Earth, return to life.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: What you talkin' about? Never heard a verse like that before.
Trusting that luck is, as ever, on her side, the challenger places the final kernel on the Tabula board.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: "Back to Earth, return to life." It's "The Butterfly"!

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: ¡Lotería!
T   h   e       T   u   r   q   u   o   i   s   e       S   e   r   p   e   n   t       C   l   u   b
Written by Recoleta
Carlota Bar
The game is decided. Disbelief ripples through the crowd.

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: Three whole days.

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: Three whole days, and this girl hasn't lost a single game, doesn't matter if it's slots, or Russian roulette, or la Lotería!

items.speaker: Gang Grunt II
items.text: She's taken down all the best gamblers in Tlazo's gang, and now she's gunnin' for the man himself.

items.speaker: Gang Grunt II
items.text: Unbelievable!

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: No, it isn't possible! You cheated!
At the center of it all, the capo sweeps everything off the table in a fury.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Ain't no such thing as "The Butterfly" card. It don't exist! What you tryna pull, huh?

items.speaker: Croupier
items.text: Sir, I-I don't know.

items.speaker: Croupier
items.text: You provided and shuffled the cards yourself.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Quit whining, sir. How many times do I have to tell you? It's all luck.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: A win is a win. There are no take-backs at the gambling table.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Besides, this is your turf. You think I'm stupid enough to cheat here of all places?

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Alright, I'll see you with my winnings this time tomorrow.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: That is, a million in chips and that thing. What was it? Something from that club of yours? Anyway, you know what it is. See you soon.
The lucky challenger laughs as she prepares to leave.
The man across the table slumps back in his chair. It's far more than he can afford to lose.

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: Mr. Tlazo, I kept my eye on her the whole time. She really didn't cheat.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Forget it. Ain't important.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Follow her. She can't make it outta here alive.
Mexico City. Sunlight falls on the low houses lining the streets.

Centurion steps out of the tavern's back alley and wanders into the street. The Day of the Dead draws near. Bone dolls, skull candies, flowers, and paper cutouts ... Vivid colors spill all the way down both sides of the road.
The dry air settles soothingly into her lungs.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: So good things really do happen when you go home, huh?

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Still got a while before the show starts. What sort of adventure can I find to kill some time?
She catches the soft rustling of feet slinking in from behind her.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Ah, speak of the devil.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Something I can help you with, gentlemen?

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: Sorry, but Tlazo ain't planning on cashing you out.
Operation codename, "The Sacrifice"? "Itzpapalotl"? "Nine Trials of Death"?
The last one has a good ring to it. I can already see the expression on the faces of those Laplace rats.
Performer: Lorentz Butterfly.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Target has entered the crossroads at Juárez Street. Activating Chaos Interference Device.

items.speaker: Rumbling Roaring Box - X
items.text: Chaos Interference Device activated.

items.speaker: Rumbling Roaring Box - X
items.text: Tip: Rumbling Roaring Box upgrade completed. Should a problem occur, please call the developer, provided you manage to survive, haha!

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Nice one, X. But what's the contact number?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Two targets, no followers.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: "Ain't no way! We gotta get backup from Mr. Tlazo!"

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: "Get her!"

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Your voice cracks, your movements hesitant. You instinctively tilt to the right and take out the knife you've kept in your inside pocket—a habit you've formed since the fight that cost you your index finger—hoping it will bring you luck.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: "STOP!!"

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Perhaps the knife does grant you courage, or you simply forgot about the shots that failed to hit the target until you saw the holes on the fence. That's when fear strikes again.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: So you halt. That's it, right where I need you to be.

items.speaker: Rumbling Roaring Box - X
items.text: Virtual environmental model constructed. All variables within predicted range.

items.speaker: Rumbling Roaring Box - X
items.text: Short-term behavior prediction possible. Conditions ideal!

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Initial condition disturbance activated.

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: W-What's that sound?

items.speaker: Gang Grunt II
items.text: Look out!
The dust settles, and a mysterious woman leaps down from the rooftop.
Centurion, unharmed and unfazed, sizes up this newcomer.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: It's you, the croupier from the bar.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Guess I owe you some thanks.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: My pleasure. I've heard of you, the legendary Coin Girl.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Even without my help, you'd have come out on top.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Hah, true, but not as easily. I could've missed tonight's show.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: So, what do you want in return? Sharpodonties? Local chow? How about a magic show? The escapes will have your jaw on the floor.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Anything but this coin. You name it, and it'll be yours by morning.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Appreciated.
She narrows her eyes, satisfied with Centurion's willingness to cooperate.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: There is something I want from you.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: It was something you won at the table: a secret letter from the Turquoise Serpent Club.
